sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned counsel for the State on the instant
interlocutory application filed by the appellant for suspension of sentence during the pendency of
this criminal appeal.

2.  This criminal appeal is directed against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 08.09.2017 and 13.09.2017 respectively passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-IV, Palamau at Daltonganj in Sessions Trial Case No.152 of 2016, arising out of Ramgarh P.S. Case No.05 of 2011 corresponding to G.R. No.376 of 2011, whereby and whereunder, the appellant has been held guilty under Sections 302, 326 and 452 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and had been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life under Section 302 of Indian Penal Code and also directed to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), rigorous imprisonment for five years and fine of Rs.3000/- under Section 326/34 of Indian Penal Code and Rigorous imprisonment for four years and fine of Rs.3,000/- for the offence under Section 452/34 of IPC.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-IV, Palamau at Daltonganj
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In default of payment of each fine, the convict was directed to undergo further imprisonment of six months of S.I. for each such default.
Half of the fine was directed to go to wife of deceased i.e., informant as compensation.
All the sentences shall run concurrently.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is making second attempt to procure the suspension of sentence.

Earlier the appellant has also filed application for suspension of sentence, which was formally rejected and therefore that may also be considered while considering the suspension of sentence of the appellant.

4. Further, at the outset, learned counsel has submitted that the appellant has been in custody since 07.11.2015 at the time of filing of the interlocutory application and therefore he has till now spend almost about 8 years 10 months in custody and this may be taken into consideration while considering the prayer for suspension of sentence.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that apart from that though 10 prosecution witnesses have been examined, but PW-1, PW-5, PW-6 and PW-8 have not supported the case of the prosecution and they have been declared hostile.
PW-2 & PW-3 are not eyewitnesses of the alleged occurrence.
PW-7 & PW-10 are doctors and PW-9 is the Investigating Officer of this case.
PW-4 is Samundari Devi, who is the wife of deceased-late Sheoraj Uraon and also the informant and has claimed to be the eyewitness of the alleged occurrence.

6. Learned counsels further submits that PW-4 in her cross- examination has deposed that the appellant as pressed the neck of the deceased but the Doctor PW-7, who conducted the autopsy, has not found any mark of ligature on his neck and hence testimony is not corroborative with the medical evidence.

He further submits that PW-4 has further in cross-examination stated about assault being made by the other two accused persons and only that this appellant has put his hand to the neck of the deceased, but as it has already been stated that it is not corroborated by the medical evidence.

He has further submitted that PW-2 and PW-8 have stated that there was darkness at the time of occurrence and therefore there was no means by which identification of any of the accused could have been made including this appellant or the manner of the assault that was made and therefore, counsel says that based on the aforesaid circumstances and also custodial period, the appellant may be granted the privilege of suspension of sentence.

7. On the other hand, learned APP appearing on behalf of the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that the conviction along with the aid of section 34 of the IPC and therefore he has been fully involved in the offence resulting in death of the deceased and therefore he will not be allowed the privilege of suspension of sentence.
2 Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1984 of 2017 8. Having heard the parties, perused the record of the case.

9. In view of the persuasive submissions advanced on behalf of the appellant and in the facts and circumstances of the case and the custody undergone by the appellant, it is found just and fair to enlarge the appellant on bail, during pendency of this criminal appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-IV, Palamau at Daltonganj in Sessions Trial Case No.152 of 2016, arising out of Ramgarh P.S. Case No.05 of 2011 corresponding to G.R. No.376 Dashrath Uraon vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15099668/
2 of 2011, subject to the conditions that the appellant will submit self-attested photocopy of his Aadhaar Card and also submit his mobile number before the learned Court below, which he will always keep active and will not change it during pendency of this case without prior permission of the Court.
